A. Overview: Why Corporate Document Translation Matters
the legal framework of a company, its governance, and decision-making processes
Errors in translation can lead to legal disputes, compliance violations, or misinterpretation of corporate rights and obligations.

2. Key Legal Terms in Corporate Law
Legally establishes a company and defines its structure
"The Articles of Incorporation were filed with the state to register the company."
"The company’s bylaws outline voting rights and management duties."
An official record of decisions made during corporate meetings
"The board secretary prepared the minutes of the annual meeting."
Defines rights and obligations of shareholders
"The shareholder agreement includes provisions on voting rights."
A formal decision made by a board of directors
Match each document with its function in
A person or entity that files the articles of incorporation
"The incorporator submitted the required documents to establish the company."
A person or service authorized to receive legal documents on behalf of a company
"The registered agent is responsible for receiving legal notices."
The governing body of a corporation
"The board of directors approved the company’s expansion plan."
The minimum number of members required for a meeting to be valid
"A quorum must be present for the board to vote on corporate matters."
The legal obligation of company officers to act in the best interest of the business
"The CEO has a fiduciary duty to the shareholders."
Identify whether each term relates to
Legal terms must reflect corporate law standards in the target jurisdiction
Some terms have no direct equivalents
between Common Law and Civil Law systems.
"The company’s bylaws establish the powers of the board of directors."
"The shareholder agreement restricts the transfer of shares."
"The minutes must accurately reflect all decisions taken during the meeting."
B. Ambiguity in Corporate Governance Documents
Corporate terms may have different legal implications
—these terms are often used interchangeably but may have different connotations.

4. Reading Practice: Corporate Documents in Context
Read the following corporate document excerpts aloud and analyze the legal terms used.
Text 1: Excerpt from Articles of Incorporation

"The corporation is formed under the laws of the State of Delaware. The initial board of directors shall consist of three members. The incorporator hereby appoints a registered agent for the purpose of receiving legal notices."

Text 2: Excerpt from Board Meeting Minutes
"The meeting was called to order at 10:00 AM with a quorum present. The board unanimously approved the resolution to issue new shares. The chairman adjourned the meeting at 11:30 AM."
What was the key decision made in the meeting?
Why is it important to record the time of adjournment?
